semantic_constraints.series: an income series is keyed by source, indicator, welfare concept (income or consumption), equivalence scale, poverty line and its PPP base year, reference-year basis, survey, coverage, methodology, area and unit; World Bank PIP, Eurostat EU-SILC and OECD IDD figures are never one series; values live in the Economics series storage (economic_vintages, dataset_observations)
semantic_constraints.definitions: each series cites its definition revision (income definition, equivalence scale, poverty line, methodology version, notes and the references the source states); a changed definition is a new revision
semantic_constraints.vintages: each release that changes a series is an appended vintage with release and retrieval clocks, revision_of and the recorded changes (new, revised and removed periods, PPP revision, definition or version change, withdrawal); a PPP revision that restates past values is a new vintage, never an overwrite; each PIP release is its own vintage; as-of answers select the vintage released by the date
semantic_constraints.comparability: sources are returned side by side, grouped by concept, welfare concept, equivalence scale, poverty line, PPP base year and reference-year basis; groups are never combined; unnoted pairs are comparability_unknown
semantic_constraints.identity: places match through reviewed mappings by ISO, NUTS and World Bank region codes before names; the same indicator across sources is recorded as related, never merged; unmatched codes stay visible
semantic_constraints.links: methodology documents, Demographics denominators and Labour indicators link by citation, shared identifier or accepted match, pointing at specific record revisions; missing providers and targets are reported
semantic_constraints.minimisation: aggregate published statistics only; no person- or household-level field is stored or returned
semantic_constraints.exclusions: no nowcasting, no filled years, no own poverty lines, no blending of PIP, EU-SILC and OECD figures into one series, no re-harmonisation of welfare concepts
